## Natural history notes

A tiny secretive wren characterized by a short cocked tail, streaked brown back, pale underside, buffy face, and thin slightly curved bill. In Florida, the Sedge Wren is mainly a winter visitor, found in wet prairies, marsh edges, sedge meadows, grassy fields, pine flatwoods, and dense low vegetation where it stays hidden near the ground. It feeds on small insects, spiders, and other invertebrates, creeping through grasses and sedges and giving short dry calls from cover.
